claim: Unfavorable redox conditions in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) can decrease the capacity for protein secretion, altering vital cell functions.
source: Unfavorable redox conditions in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) can decrease the capacity for protein secretion, altering vital cell functions.
evidence: This is a general statement about ER redox conditions and protein secretion, drawing from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The chaperone BiP is a sensor of overly oxidizing ER conditions.
source: In previous work (Wang et al., 2014), we demonstrated that the chaperone BiP is a sensor of overly oxidizing ER conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Modification of a conserved BiP cysteine during stress beneficially alters BiP chaperone activity to cope with suboptimal folding conditions.
source: We showed that modification of a conserved BiP cysteine during stress beneficially alters BiP chaperone activity to cope with suboptimal folding conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors (Wang et al., 2014).

claim: BiP's nucleotide exchange factor – Sil1 – can reverse BiP cysteine oxidation.
source: Here we demonstrate that BiP's nucleotide exchange factor – Sil1 – can reverse BiP cysteine oxidation.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by multiple experimental data presented in the results section.

claim: Yeast Sil1 has reductant capacity.
source: This previously unexpected reductant capacity for yeast Sil1 has potential implications for the human ataxia Marinesco-Sjögren syndrome
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing Sil1's ability to reduce oxidized BiP.

claim: A disruption in ER redox-signaling due to genetic defects in SIL1 may influence Marinesco-Sjögren syndrome disease pathology.
source: where it is interesting to speculate that a disruption in ER redox-signaling (due to genetic defects in SIL1) may influence disease pathology.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: The oxidizing environment of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) facilitates the folding and secretion of approximately a third of the cellular proteome.
source: In eukaryotes, the oxidizing environment of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) facilitates the folding and secretion of approximately a third of the cellular proteome.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the ER.

claim: Transient increases in oxidative folding both deplete reduced glutathione and generate hydrogen peroxide.
source: Protein flux through the ER varies widely, and transient increases in oxidative folding both deplete reduced glutathione and generate hydrogen peroxide, which can disrupt protein structure, folding, and secretion (Bulleid and Ellgaard, 2011; Kakihana et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Hydrogen peroxide can disrupt protein structure, folding, and secretion.
source: Protein flux through the ER varies widely, and transient increases in oxidative folding both deplete reduced glutathione and generate hydrogen peroxide, which can disrupt protein structure, folding, and secretion (Bulleid and Ellgaard, 2011; Kakihana et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A conserved cysteine in the nucleotide-binding domain of the Hsp70 chaperone BiP (Kar2) senses alterations in levels of both glutathione and peroxide in the ER.
source: We have shown in yeast that a conserved cysteine in the nucleotide-binding domain of the Hsp70 chaperone BiP (Kar2) senses alterations in levels of both glutathione and peroxide in the ER.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: As ER levels of glutathione and peroxide rise, the BiP cysteine becomes oxidized, converting the normally ATP-driven chaperone into an ATP-independent protein holdase.
source: As ER levels of these small molecules rise, the BiP cysteine becomes oxidized, converting the normally ATP-driven chaperone into an ATP-independent protein holdase (Wang et al., 2014; Wang and Sevier, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: In mammals, formation of an intramolecular disulfide bond in BiP in the presence of increased oxidants augments BiP chaperone function.
source: A similar system has been proposed for mammals, where formation of an intramolecular disulfide bond in the presence of increased oxidants augments BiP chaperone function (Wei et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The increased chaperone activity of oxidized BiP is proposed to promote cell survival by limiting polypeptide aggregation during suboptimal folding conditions.
source: The increased chaperone activity of oxidized BiP is proposed to promote cell survival by limiting polypeptide aggregation during suboptimal folding conditions (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The ER contains multiple members of the thioredoxin superfamily with the capacity to reduce oxidized thiols.
source: The ER contains multiple members of the thioredoxin superfamily with the capacity to reduce oxidized thiols
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ER reductases.

claim: The relatively buried location of the redox-sensitive cysteine in BiP suggests that BiP is a poor candidate substrate for thioredoxin superfamily reductases.
source: yet the relatively buried location of the redox-sensitive cysteine in BiP suggests that BiP is a poor candidate substrate for these reductases.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural considerations of BiP.

claim: Sil1 is an unexpected reductant of oxidized BiP.
source: Here we identify Sil1, BiP's nucleotide exchange factor (NEF), as an unexpected reductant of oxidized BiP.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by experimental data.

claim: A redox-active cysteine pair within a flexible N-terminal polypeptide domain of Sil1 facilitates reduction of the relatively buried BiP cysteine.
source: We propose that a redox-active cysteine pair within a flexible N-terminal polypeptide domain of Sil1 facilitates reduction of the relatively buried BiP cysteine.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental data and structural considerations.

claim: A yeast strain unable to undergo BiP oxidation (a kar2-C63A strain) was inviable when cells were subject to oxidative ER stress.
source: This screen took advantage of our prior observations that (i) a yeast strain unable to undergo BiP oxidation (a kar2-C63A strain) was inviable when cells were subject to oxidative ER stress
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: An ectopic BiP allele that functionally mimics oxidized BiP allows for robust growth of the compromised kar2-C63A strain.
source: and (ii) an ectopic BiP allele that functionally mimics oxidized BiP allows for robust growth of the compromised kar2-C63A strain (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The BiP-K314E mutation does not compromise essential BiP activity.
source: We observed that the K314E mutation does not compromise essential BiP activity; a BiP-K314E allele can support cell viability as the sole cellular BiP (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A strain containing a BiP-K314E mutant was able to more efficiently manage oxidative stress, exhibiting a greater resistance to the small molecule oxidant diamide.
source: Yet, in keeping with the original screen design, a strain containing a BiP-K314E mutant was able to more efficiently manage oxidative stress, exhibiting a greater resistance to the small molecule oxidant diamide (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: BiP Cys63 and Lys314 are both located in the BiP ATPase domain.
source: The redox-active BiP cysteine (Cys63) and Lys314 are both located in the BiP ATPase domain
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge of BiP.

claim: Cys63 is relatively hidden within a cleft that forms the nucleotide-binding pocket.
source: Cys63 is relatively hidden within a cleft that forms the nucleotide-binding pocket
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge of BiP, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lys314 is surface exposed, found at the interface formed between BiP and its NEF Sil1.
source: while Lys314 is surface exposed, found at the interface formed between BiP and its NEF Sil1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Yan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on structural data from prior literature and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is a clear disruption in the physical association between Sil1 and recombinant BiP-K314E.
source: Using a GST-pulldown assay, we confirmed a clear disruption in the physical association between Sil1 and recombinant BiP-K314E (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A strain lacking both NEFs (lhs1∆ sil1∆) is inviable.
source: BiP utilizes two NEFs, and a strain lacking both NEFs (lhs1∆ sil1∆) is inviable (Tyson and Stirling, 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A BiP-K314E allele behaved like a sil1∆ allele, showing inviability in combination with lhs1∆.
source: a BiP-K314E allele behaved like a sil1∆ allele, showing inviability in combination with lhs1∆ (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The resistance to diamide conferred by the K314E mutation was largely abolished upon mutation of BiP Cys63 (a C63A-K314E mutation).
source: Yet, while such a mechanism may contribute to some of the beneficial impact of the BiP-K314E allele during stress, we observed that the resistance to diamide conferred by the K314E mutation was largely abolished upon mutation of BiP Cys63 (a C63A-K314E mutation; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A BiP-K314E allele enhanced the recovery of oxidized BiP from stressed cells.
source: Strikingly, a BiP-K314E allele further enhanced the recovery of oxidized BiP from stressed cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C using the biotin-switch assay.

claim: A sil1∆ strain accumulated more oxidized BiP than a wild-type strain under stress.
source: Indeed, a sil1∆ strain not only accumulated more oxidized BiP than a wild-type strain under stress but also showed a higher basal level of oxidized BiP in the absence of stressor (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: A sil1∆ strain showed a higher basal level of oxidized BiP in the absence of stressor.
source: Indeed, a sil1∆ strain not only accumulated more oxidized BiP than a wild-type strain under stress but also showed a higher basal level of oxidized BiP in the absence of stressor (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: A sil1∆ strain exhibited an increased ability to survive in the presence of diamide, relative to a wild-type strain.
source: A sil1∆ strain also exhibited an increased ability to survive in the presence of diamide, relative to a wild-type strain (Figure 1E)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The resistance of a sil1∆ strain to diamide was lessened when the BiP cysteine was mutated to alanine.
source: In keeping with this model, the resistance of a sil1∆ strain to diamide was lessened when the BiP cysteine was mutated to alanine (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A sil1∆ kar2-C63A strain displays more resistance to diamide than a kar2-C63A strain.
source: However, it is important to note that the increased diamide resistance observed for the sil1∆ strain cannot be attributed exclusively to a role for Sil1 in modulating BiP's redox state; a sil1∆ kar2-C63A strain displays more resistance to diamide than a kar2-C63A strain (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: When stress conditions subside, the BiP cysteine-adduct is reduced (removed) with a half-life of less than 10 min.
source: We have shown previously that when stress conditions subside, the BiP cysteine-adduct is reduced (removed) with a half-life of less than 10 min (Wang and Sevier, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: A rapid decrease in oxidized BiP levels in a wild-type strain post-oxidant removal was observed (t1/2 ~6 min).
source: Utilizing the biotin-switch assay, we observed a rapid decrease in oxidized BiP levels in a wild-type strain post-oxidant removal (t1/2 ~6 min) (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: The stability of the BiP cysteine-adduct was markedly enhanced in a strain lacking Sil1 (sil1∆), demonstrating a half-life of greater than 45 min.
source: In contrast, the stability of the BiP cysteine-adduct was markedly enhanced in a strain lacking Sil1 (sil1∆), demonstrating a half-life of greater than 45 min (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: Sil1 has been implicated in the retro-translocation of cholera toxin.
source: Sil1 has been implicated in the retro-translocation of cholera toxin (Williams et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The level of oxidized BiP in a sil1∆ strain was restored to wild-type levels 1 hr post-oxidant removal.
source: Of note, the level of oxidized BiP in a sil1∆ strain was restored to wild-type levels 1 hr post-oxidant removal (Figure 1F,G), demonstrating that other (slower) mechanisms exist for BiP reduction in the absence of Sil1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: Other (slower) mechanisms exist for BiP reduction in the absence of Sil1.
source: Of note, the level of oxidized BiP in a sil1∆ strain was restored to wild-type levels 1 hr post-oxidant removal (Figure 1F,G), demonstrating that other (slower) mechanisms exist for BiP reduction in the absence of Sil1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing BiP reduction in sil1∆ cells.

claim: A strain containing a mimetic allele of constitutively oxidized BiP (as the sole copy of cellular BiP) is inviable under non-stress conditions.
source: we have shown previously that a strain containing a mimetic allele of constitutively oxidized BiP (as the sole copy of cellular BiP) is inviable under non-stress conditions (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Sil1 contains a pair of cysteines in the N-terminal domain separated by four intervening residues (Cys-52 and Cys-57).
source: However, we were struck by the presence of a pair of cysteines in the N-terminal domain of Sil1 separated by four intervening residues (Cys-52 and Cys-57)
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of Sil1.

claim: Sil1 reduced the otherwise stable BiP-TNB adduct.
source: Strikingly, Sil1 reduced the otherwise stable BiP-TNB adduct (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Sil1 reducing activity required the presence of either Cys52 or Cys57; a C52A-C57A mutant showed no capacity to facilitate BiP reduction.
source: Sil1 reducing activity required the presence of either Cys52 or Cys57; a C52A-C57A mutant showed no capacity to facilitate BiP reduction (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The presence of a single N-terminal cysteine (either Cys-52 or Cys-57) was sufficient to release TNB.
source: Interestingly, the presence of a single N-terminal cysteine (either Cys-52 or Cys-57) was sufficient to release TNB, demonstrating that each cysteine can act as the attacking nucleophile (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Each cysteine (Cys-52 or Cys-57) can act as the attacking nucleophile.
source: Interestingly, the presence of a single N-terminal cysteine (either Cys-52 or Cys-57) was sufficient to release TNB, demonstrating that each cysteine can act as the attacking nucleophile (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing TNB release with single cysteine mutants.

claim: In thioredoxin, only the first cysteine in the active site Cys-X-X-Cys motif is able to serve as an attacking nucleophile.
source: Such a mechanism is distinct from that used by the well-characterized reductase thioredoxin, where only the first cysteine in the active site Cys-X-X-Cys motif is able to serve as an attacking nucleophile (Lu and Holmgren, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Enzymes containing redox-active cysteine pairs that do not adopt a thioredoxin fold have shown a behavior similar to what is seen with Sil1, including the ER-localized oxidase Erv2.
source: However enzymes containing redox-active cysteine pairs that do not adopt a thioredoxin fold have shown a behavior similar to what is seen with Sil1, including the ER-localized oxidase Erv2 (Gross et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Sil1 contains two additional cysteines within the armadillo repeats (Cys-203 and Cys-373).
source: Sil1 contains two additional cysteines within the armadillo repeats (Cys-203 and Cys-373)
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of Sil1.

claim: The cysteines Cys-203 and Cys-373 were dispensable for Sil1 reducing activity.
source: we observed that these cysteines were dispensable for Sil1 reducing activity (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GSH showed negligible activity when tested at an equivalent concentration to Sil1.
source: Surprisingly, GSH showed negligible activity when tested at an equivalent concentration to Sil1 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A 100-fold excess of GSH was required to recapitulate comparable Sil1 activity.
source: In fact, a 100-fold excess of GSH was required to recapitulate comparable Sil1 activity (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The high affinity reported for Sil1 towards BiP likely accounts for the increased reducing capacity observed for Sil1 relative to GSH.
source: We expect that the high affinity reported for Sil1 towards BiP likely accounts for the increased reducing capacity observed for Sil1 relative to GSH (Yan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on known binding affinity and experimental data.

claim: BiP transitioned from an oxidized to a reduced form in the presence of Sil1-C203A-C373A.
source: Consistent with the TNB release observed spectroscopically (Figure 2B), treatment with mal-PEG2K indicated that BiP transitioned from an oxidized (Figure 2D, lane 8) to a reduced form (Figure 2D, lane 11) in the presence of Sil1-C203A-C373A.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Sil1 concomitantly transitioned from a reduced to oxidized state during BiP reduction.
source: Importantly, in keeping with the proposed thiol-disulfide exchange reaction, Sil1 concomitantly transitioned from a reduced (Figure 2D, lane 8) to oxidized (Figure 2D, lane 11) state.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The oxidation state of BiP-TNB did not change when BiP-TNB was reacted with Sil1 lacking the N-terminal cysteine pair.
source: The oxidation state of BiP-TNB did not change when BiP-TNB was reacted with Sil1 lacking the N-terminal cysteine pair, confirming that the N-terminal cysteines are necessary for efficient BiP-TNB reduction (Figure 2D, lane 9 and 12).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A transient high molecular weight band consistent with a BiP-Sil1 mixed-disulfide intermediate was observed upon incubation of BiP-TNB and Sil1-C203A-C373A.
source: A transient high molecular weight band was also observed upon incubation of BiP-TNB and Sil1-C203A-C373A (Figure 2D, asterisk). The molecular weight of this band is consistent with a BiP-Sil1 mixed-disulfide intermediate (Figure 2A, asterisk)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The formation of the BiP-Sil1 mixed-disulfide band was rapid and readily apparent immediately upon mixing.
source: and interestingly the formation of the band was rapid and readily apparent immediately upon mixing (Figure 2D, t = 0, lane 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Use of a Sil1 single cysteine mutant (Sil1-C52A or -C57A) as reductant enhanced recovery of the mixed-disulfide species.
source: Use of a Sil1 single cysteine mutant (Sil1-C52A or -C57A) as reductant enhanced recovery of the mixed-disulfide species (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Sil1 was able to remove the glutathione adduct from BiP.
source: We observed that Sil1 was able to remove the glutathione adduct from BiP, which was evident in the appearance of the slower migrating reduced BiP species over time (Figure 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The reduction of the BiP glutathione adduct was dependent on the presence of the Sil1 N-terminal cysteines.
source: and that the reduction of the BiP glutathione adduct was dependent on the presence of the Sil1 N-terminal cysteines (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Removal of the glutathione adduct from BiP was coincident with the oxidation of the Sil1 N-terminal cysteines.
source: Removal of the glutathione adduct from BiP was coincident with the oxidation of the Sil1 N-terminal cysteines, which was indicated by the appearance of a faster migrating Sil1 species over time (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A strain possessing a sil1-C52A-C57A allele demonstrated the same sensitivity to diamide as a wild-type strain.
source: In contrast, we observed that a strain possessing a sil1-C52A-C57A allele demonstrated the same sensitivity to diamide as a wild-type strain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of the active-site cysteines does not influence NEF activity.
source: We observed that the presence of the active-site cysteines does not influence NEF activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The inviability of a lhs1∆ sil1∆ strain was rescued by a Sil1 catalytic-cysteine mutant.
source: The inviability of a lhs1∆ sil1∆ strain (ascribed to a loss of NEF function) was rescued by a Sil1 catalytic-cysteine mutant (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Both wild-type Sil1 and Sil1-C52A-C57A stimulated ATP turnover by BiP.
source: Furthermore, both wild-type Sil1 and Sil1-C52A-C57A stimulated ATP turnover by BiP (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Sil1-H163E is defective in BiP binding.
source: Sil1-H163E is defective in BiP binding (Yan et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Sil1-H163E is ineffective as a NEF and a reductant.
source: and as a consequence is ineffective as a NEF and a reductant (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 4A,B.

claim: Recombinant oxidized BiP shows a lower steady-state ATPase rate than reduced BiP.
source: We have shown previously that recombinant oxidized BiP shows a lower steady-state ATPase rate than reduced BiP (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Only a Sil1 protein with reducing activity (wild-type Sil1) in combination with a reversible BiP-TNB substrate allowed for measurable BiP ATPase activity.
source: When Sil1 activity was assessed in the context of modified BiP, we observed that only a Sil1 protein with reducing activity (wild-type Sil1) in combination with a reversible BiP-TNB substrate allowed for measurable BiP ATPase activity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Reduction of BiP-TNB by Sil1 reversed the enhanced holdase activity associated with modified BiP.
source: Correspondingly, reduction of BiP-TNB by Sil1 reversed the enhanced holdase activity also associated with modified BiP (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: BiP-TNB limited the aggregation of denatured rhodanese relative to unmodified BiP.
source: Consistent with our prior reports (Wang et al., 2014), BiP-TNB limited the aggregation of denatured rhodanese relative to unmodified BiP, evident as a decrease in light scattering observed in the presence of BiP-TNB relative to unmodified BiP (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and citation to prior work.

claim: A BiP/J-protein/Sil1 protein mixture shows a lower steady-state ATPase rate relative to a BiP/J-protein/Lhs1 combination.
source: It has been shown previously that a BiP/J-protein/Sil1 protein mixture shows a lower steady-state ATPase rate relative to a BiP/J-protein/Lhs1 combination (Steel et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Sil1 only modestly enhanced steady-state BiP ATPase activity relative to Lhs1.
source: We observed also that Sil1 only modestly enhanced steady-state BiP ATPase activity relative to Lhs1, which was used at an even lower concentration than Sil1 (Figure 4E, left panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Lhs1 was unable to stimulate the ATPase rate of BiP-TNB.
source: Focusing on modified BiP, we found that Lhs1 was unable to stimulate the ATPase rate of BiP-TNB, suggesting that Lhs1 is not active as a reductant.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Lhs1 is not active as a reductant.
source: Focusing on modified BiP, we found that Lhs1 was unable to stimulate the ATPase rate of BiP-TNB, suggesting that Lhs1 is not active as a reductant. Low reducing activity was observed also when TNB release was monitored spectroscopically (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data showing lack of ATPase stimulation and low TNB release.

claim: Sil1 reducing activity is specific to Sil1 and not a common feature of the ER NEFs.
source: These data imply that Sil1 reducing activity is specific to Sil1 and not a common feature of the ER NEFs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of Sil1 and Lhs1 activities.

claim: Human SIL1 shows functional and structural conservation with yeast Sil1.
source: Human SIL1 shows functional and structural conservation with yeast Sil1
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about SIL1 orthologs.

claim: Human and yeast SIL1 share limited primary sequence homology.
source: however, they share limited primary sequence homology (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mammalian and yeast BiP exhibit a high degree of sequence conservation.
source: This is in contrast to mammalian and yeast BiP, which exhibit a high degree of sequence conservation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The N-terminal domain of human SIL1 contains a pair of cysteine residues, which is highly conserved between the mammalian SIL1 orthologs.
source: Yet strikingly, the N-terminal domain of human SIL1 contains a pair of cysteine residues, which is highly conserved between the mammalian SIL1 orthologs (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 5.

claim: The location and spacing of cysteines in human SIL1 is similar to location and spacing of the redox-active cysteines in yeast Sil1.
source: The location and spacing of these cysteines in human SIL1 is similar to location and spacing of the redox-active cysteines in yeast Sil1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cysteine conservation likely speaks to an important structural or functional role for these mammalian SIL1 cysteines.
source: Cysteine is a rare amino acid in proteins, and cysteine conservation likely speaks to an important structural or functional role for these mammalian SIL1 cysteines (Marino and Gladyshev, 2010).
evidence: This is an inference based on the rarity of cysteine and conservation patterns, supported by citation.

claim: Mutations in human SIL1 are associated with Marinesco-Sjögren syndrome (MSS).
source: Mutations in human SIL1 are associated with Marinesco-Sjögren syndrome (MSS), an autosomal recessive disorder arising in early childhood that manifests in musculoskeletal defects, cognitive delay, and early onset cataracts (Senderek et al., 2005; Anttonen et al., 2005; Krieger et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MSS is an autosomal recessive disorder arising in early childhood that manifests in musculoskeletal defects, cognitive delay, and early onset cataracts.
source: Mutations in human SIL1 are associated with Marinesco-Sjögren syndrome (MSS), an autosomal recessive disorder arising in early childhood that manifests in musculoskeletal defects, cognitive delay, and early onset cataracts (Senderek et al., 2005; Anttonen et al., 2005; Krieger et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: SIL1 has been described as a modifier of the neurodegenerative disorder ALS.
source: Recently, a new role for SIL1 as a modifier of the neurodegenerative disorder ALS has also been described (de Keyzer et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A majority of MSS alleles are truncations and deletions.
source: A majority of MSS alleles are truncations and deletions (Goto et al., 2014; Ezgu et al., 2014; Krieger et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MSS truncations and deletions will impact reducing activity while also destroying NEF function.
source: which will impact reducing activity while also destroying NEF function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nature of truncations and deletions.

claim: 50% of MSS patients have no SIL1 defect and no characterized genetic cause.
source: We speculate that the identification of physiological reductants for Sil1 may also point toward new candidate genetic mutations that account for the onset of disease in the 50% of MSS patients without any SIL1 defect and no characterized genetic cause.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about MSS patients.

claim: Yeast BiP contains a single cysteine (Cys63).
source: Yeast BiP contains a single cysteine (Cys63), and any avidin signal in this switch assay has been traced to Cys63 oxidation (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and prior work by the authors.

claim: Any avidin signal in the biotin-switch assay has been traced to Cys63 oxidation.
source: Yeast BiP contains a single cysteine (Cys63), and any avidin signal in this switch assay has been traced to Cys63 oxidation (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Approximately two-fold more oxidized BiP was recovered from cells grown under conditions of ER stress.
source: Confirming our prior results, approximately two-fold more oxidized BiP was recovered from cells grown under conditions of ER stress (Figure 1C) (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and citation to prior work.

claim: Sil1 His163 has been shown to be critically involved in the association of Sil1 with BiP.
source: Sil1 His163 has been shown to be critically involved in the association of Sil1 with BiP (Yan et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A Sil1-H163E mutant was unable to effectively reduce BiP-TNB.
source: and we observed that a Sil1-H163E mutant was unable to effectively reduce BiP-TNB (Figure 2B).
